=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:965-975 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `final_ci_in_flight` branch (`if [ -z "${verdict_wait_reason}" ] && [ "${approved_final_ci}" = "in_flight" ]`) does not check `.mergeable == "MERGEABLE"`, unlike `review_sweep_verdict_wait_reason` (scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh line 418), so an approved head that is CONFLICTING or UNKNOWN is skipped while its final CI is queued or running.
  WHY: The README row for `VERDICT_WAIT_DISPATCH_SKIP_ENABLED` and `agents.d/9991-verdict-wait-dispatch-skip.md` promise that "a conflicted or not yet computed head is dispatched", so the conflict is not re-reviewed until the CI run finishes (a delay bounded by the CI run time); four reviewers rated this NIT and gemini gave no severity, so low is the highest stated; minimal fix is to add `&& printf '%s' "${row}" | jq -e '.mergeable == "MERGEABLE"' >/dev/null 2>&1` to the condition.
- scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:499-520 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `review_sweep_verdict_wait_alert` sends the Telegram alert (`tg_send_msg`) before it writes the once-per-head `ai-review/verdict-wait-alert` status marker, so if every marker POST attempt fails (`outcome=marker_failed`), the next tick finds no marker and sends the alert again.
  WHY: This breaks G3's "raised once per head, not once per tick" whenever the marker POST fails, and no test covers that path (only `test_failed_send_posts_no_marker` exists); severity disagreement: minimax and openai rated MAJOR and anthropic rated NIT (the retries narrow the window and the order fails toward alerting), so the highest (MAJOR) is used; z-ai_glm-5_3-flash treated the triple-failure residual as fail-open and did not re-flag it.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:951-981 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The `final_ci_merge_pending` skip (label `ai:final-ci-merge-pending`) reaches `continue` at line 979 without the `merge_train_skip_active` guard that the lease-wait skip at line 839 has, so it holds the PR even when `MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED` is off.
  WHY: Only `_mt_final_ci_merge_resume` (scripts/review_merge_train.sh line 3206) removes the label and merges the PR, and scripts/review_merge_train.sh lines 205-210 exit 0 when the train is disabled, so a labelled approved mergeable head is skipped on every tick and never merged; source severity MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "§15, API budget: no new per-PR call inside the sweep loop or the stall loop. Use data those loops already hold... If one more read is unavoidable, batch it and document the count in the function header." (issue #9991, Constraints)
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh, `review_sweep_verdict_wait_alert` (and its per-skipped-PR call sites in .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The alert helper is called per skipped PR (.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml line 977 per anthropic/openai, :843 per gemini, both the merge-lease-wait and verdict-wait branches per minimax), and for checks-blocked heads it calls `_pr_ruleset_required_check_blockers` per head at scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh lines 480-488 / 481–488 / 482-484 (one to three API reads per openai). The lease branch makes its own `_merge_lease_read` (minimax). Ruleset blockers are not batched or cached, and the read repeats each tick when the send was `not_delivered` or the marker POST failed (anthropic). The function header does document the count ("at most one blocker read set ... per head, once"), but there is no batched prefetch. Severity disagreement: anthropic rated NIT with confidence 2; gemini, minimax and openai rated MAJOR with confidence 5. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash judged the gap covered by the issue's fallback clause and did not flag it.
- requirement: "No new per-PR call inside the sweep loop or the stall loop"; if another read is unavoidable, "batch it and document the count in the function header."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_rb_judge_verdict_wait_check
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Stall recovery runs one GraphQL read per waiting PR at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:33257-33258 and does not batch it into a cycle-level prefetch.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:lines 951-981 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `review_sweep_verdict_wait_reason` returns `final_ci_merge_pending` for a labelled approved head, and that path reaches `continue` at line 979 with no merge-train guard (the lease-wait skip at line 839 runs only when `merge_train_skip_active` is `true`). The `ai:final-ci-merge-pending` skip therefore does not depend on `MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED`, but only `_mt_final_ci_merge_resume` (scripts/review_merge_train.sh line 3206) removes the label, and scripts/review_merge_train.sh lines 205-210 exit 0 when the train is off. `_pr_final_ci_merge_pending_mark` (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh lines 5277 and 5282) names "the review sweep still retries" as the fallback.
  WHY: With `MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED=false` and verdict-wait on, a labelled approved mergeable PR keeps the label for good. It is skipped every tick as `verdict_wait detail=final_ci_merge_pending` and stays open until a person acts, and the single alert wrongly says "final CI queued or running". Fix: add the `merge_train_skip_active` condition, or return `final_ci_merge_pending` only while the train is enabled.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:lines 971-972, `if [ -z "${verdict_wait_reason}" ] && [ "${approved_final_ci}" = "in_flight" ]; then verdict_wait_reason="final_ci_in_flight"` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `final_ci_in_flight` does not check `.mergeable == "MERGEABLE"` (scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh line 418 does), so CONFLICTING or UNKNOWN heads fall through and are skipped while a final CI is in flight.
  WHY: This contradicts the README and agents.d statement "a conflicted or not yet computed head is dispatched". The delay is bounded by the CI run time. One-line jq mergeable fix.
- scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:`review_sweep_verdict_wait_alert`, lines 499-520 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The alert is sent before its once-per-head marker is written. If every marker POST attempt fails, the next tick re-alerts.
  WHY: The repeat happens only while the status POST keeps failing. Retries narrow the window, the order fails toward alerting, and `marker_failed` is logged. This is a duplicate-alert nit, not a broken invariant.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "§15, API budget: no new per-PR call inside the sweep loop ... If one more read is unavoidable, batch it and document the count in the function header."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh, `review_sweep_verdict_wait_alert`, called per skipped PR at .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml line 977
  Evidence of absence: The helper calls `_pr_ruleset_required_check_blockers` once per checks-blocked head (lines 480-488). Lease holders are cached but blockers are not batched or cached. The header documents the count, and the read happens only after the threshold with Telegram configured. The read is still not batched, and it repeats every tick after a `not_delivered` send or a failed marker POST.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:the verdict-wait block, ~lines 965-975 (the `final_ci_in_flight` branch and the subsequent skip) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `review_sweep_verdict_wait_reason` requires `.mergeable == "MERGEABLE"`, but the `final_ci_in_flight` branch sets the reason from `approved_final_ci` alone. A CONFLICTING approved head with an in-flight final CI is skipped under `AUTOFIX_SWEEP_SKIP ... reason=verdict_wait detail=final_ci_in_flight`.
  WHY: The dispatched re-review is what resolves a conflict, so the head is silently held until the CI finishes. This contradicts the documented behaviour and adds latency.
- scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:review_sweep_verdict_wait_alert, the `tg_send_msg` call followed by the `gh api ... /statuses/${vwa_sha}` retry loop | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Telegram is sent before the marker is written. If all 3 `gh_retry`/plain `gh` attempts fail, `outcome=marker_failed` is logged, the next tick sees no `verdict_wait_alerted`, and it re-alerts. No test covers this path; only `test_failed_send_posts_no_marker` exists.
  WHY: This violates G3 of issue #9991 ("raised once per head, not once per tick") and creates operator alert noise. Write the marker first so it is the gate.
